medicines.name: Paracetamol
medicines.usage: Used to treat mild to moderate pain (headaches, toothache, muscle pain) and reduce fever.
medicines.dosage: Adults: 1-2 tablets every 4-6 hours as needed. Do not exceed 4g (8 tablets) per day.
warnings: May cause liver damage if taken in excessive amounts.
Do not mix with alcohol.
Overdose can be fatal — seek emergency help immediately.
Avoid in severe liver or kidney disease.
medicines.storage: Store at room temperature (15-25°C), away from moisture and direct light

medicines.name: Amoxicillin
medicines.usage: Used to treat a wide variety of bacterial infections including ear, nose, throat, skin, and urinary tract infections.
medicines.dosage: Adults: 250-500mg every 8 hours or 500-875mg every 12 hours. Complete the full course prescribed.
warnings: May cause severe allergic reactions in individuals allergic to penicillin.
Can decrease the effectiveness of birth control pills.
Avoid if history of mononucleosis.
Not effective against viral infections.
medicines.storage: Store in cool, dry place. Liquid form must be refrigerated and used within 14 days.

medicines.name: Ibuprofen
medicines.usage: Used for pain relief (headache, dental pain, menstrual cramps, arthritis), fever reduction, and inflammation.
medicines.dosage: Adults: 1-2 tablets (200-400mg) every 4-6 hours. Maximum 1200mg per day (OTC) or up to 3200mg/day under medical supervision.
warnings: May cause stomach ulcers or bleeding with prolonged use.
Avoid if pregnant, especially in third trimester.
Increases cardiovascular risk with long-term use.
Avoid with kidney disease.
medicines.storage: Store at room temperature, away from moisture

medicines.name: Aspirin
medicines.usage: Used for pain relief, fever reduction, and blood thinning (prevention of heart attacks and strokes).
medicines.dosage: Pain/fever: 325-650mg every 4-6 hours (max 4g/day). Cardiac: 75-100mg daily.
warnings: Increases bleeding risk.
Avoid in children under 16 (Reye's syndrome risk).
Avoid if allergic to NSAIDs.
May worsen asthma.
medicines.storage: Store away from moisture and heat

medicines.name: Metformin
medicines.usage: Used to manage type 2 diabetes by lowering blood glucose levels. Also used for prediabetes and PCOS.
medicines.dosage: Start: 500mg once or twice daily with meals. Gradually increase to max 2000-2550mg/day.
warnings: Risk of lactic acidosis in kidney disease.
Not for type 1 diabetes.
Avoid before surgery or contrast dye procedures.
Hold if significant illness.
side_effects: Vitamin B12 deficiency with long-term use
medicines.storage: Store at room temperature, away from moisture

medicines.name: Lisinopril
medicines.usage: Used to manage high blood pressure, heart failure, and to protect kidneys in diabetic patients.
medicines.dosage: High blood pressure: 10-40mg once daily. Heart failure: Start 2.5-5mg, titrate up.
warnings: May cause dizziness, especially on first dose.
Absolutely avoid during pregnancy (teratogenic).
Risk of hyperkalemia.
Angioedema risk — stop immediately if facial swelling.
medicines.storage: Store at room temperature

medicines.name: Omeprazole
medicines.usage: Used to reduce stomach acid and treat acid reflux (GERD), peptic ulcers, and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome.
medicines.dosage: 1 capsule (20mg) daily before breakfast. For ulcers: 20-40mg daily for 4-8 weeks.
warnings: Long-term use may reduce vitamin B12, magnesium, and calcium absorption.
Increased fracture risk with prolonged use.
May mask symptoms of gastric cancer.
Clostridioides difficile risk.
medicines.storage: Store at room temperature in original packaging

medicines.name: Atorvastatin
medicines.usage: Used to reduce cholesterol (LDL) and triglycerides, and to lower heart disease and stroke risk.
medicines.dosage: 10-80mg once daily, usually in the evening. Dose depends on LDL target and risk factors.
warnings: May cause myopathy or rhabdomyolysis (muscle breakdown).
Avoid during pregnancy.
Regular liver function monitoring needed.
Avoid grapefruit juice (increases drug levels).
medicines.storage: Store at room temperature

medicines.name: Levothyroxine
medicines.usage: Used to treat hypothyroidism (underactive thyroid) and replace or provide more thyroid hormone.
medicines.dosage: 1 tablet daily on empty stomach, 30-60 minutes before food. Dose adjusted by TSH monitoring.
warnings: Must maintain consistent brand/manufacturer.
Avoid taking with calcium, iron, antacids within 4 hours.
Pregnancy requires dose adjustment.
May worsen cardiac arrhythmias.
medicines.storage: Store at room temperature, away from light and moisture

medicines.name: Cetirizine
medicines.usage: Used to treat allergic rhinitis (hay fever), allergic conjunctivitis, hives, and other allergy symptoms.
medicines.dosage: Adults: 10mg once daily or 5mg twice daily. May take with or without food.
warnings: May cause drowsiness in some people.
Avoid with alcohol.
Dose adjustment needed in kidney disease.
Use caution while driving.
medicines.storage: Store at room temperature

medicines.name: Azithromycin
medicines.usage: Used to treat bacterial infections including pneumonia, bronchitis, sinusitis, sexually transmitted infections (chlamydia), and skin infections.
medicines.dosage: Community-acquired pneumonia: 500mg day 1, then 250mg days 2-5. STIs: single 1g dose.
warnings: May cause potentially fatal irregular heart rhythm (QT prolongation).
Use with caution in liver disease.
May cause C. difficile diarrhea.
Not effective against viral infections.
medicines.storage: Store below 30°C

medicines.name: Diclofenac
medicines.usage: Used to treat pain, inflammation, and stiffness associated with arthritis, muscle pain, gout, and menstrual cramps.
medicines.dosage: 50mg 2-3 times daily or 75mg twice daily. Take with food to reduce GI side effects.
warnings: Increased risk of heart attack and stroke.
May cause stomach ulcers or bleeding.
Avoid in last trimester of pregnancy.
Risk of kidney problems.
medicines.storage: Store below 30°C, away from moisture

medicines.name: Pantoprazole
medicines.usage: Used to treat erosive esophagitis, GERD, and conditions that cause excess stomach acid (Zollinger-Ellison syndrome).
medicines.dosage: 40mg once daily before a meal, for 4-8 weeks.
warnings: Long-term use may cause vitamin B12 and magnesium deficiency.
May increase risk of bone fractures.
Not recommended for long-term use without medical supervision.
medicines.storage: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture

medicines.name: Ciprofloxacin
medicines.usage: Used to treat a wide variety of bacterial infections including UTIs, respiratory infections, skin infections, and anthrax.
medicines.dosage: 250-750mg twice daily, depending on infection type and severity.
warnings: Risk of tendon damage and rupture (especially Achilles tendon).
May cause peripheral neuropathy.
Avoid excessive sun exposure (photosensitivity).
Not for children under 18 except specific indications.
medicines.storage: Store at room temperature, away from light

medicines.name: Clotrimazole
medicines.usage: Used to treat fungal infections including athlete's foot, jock itch, ringworm, oral thrush, and vaginal thrush.
medicines.dosage: Cream: Apply 2-3 times daily for 2-4 weeks. Pessary: Insert at bedtime for 3-6 nights.
warnings: For external use only (cream form).
Avoid contact with eyes.
Inform doctor if symptoms don't improve in 4 weeks.
May damage latex condoms and diaphragms.
interactions: Tacrolimus (systemic interactions rare with topical use)
medicines.storage: Store below 25°C, do not freeze

medicines.name: Hydrocortisone
medicines.usage: Used to relieve itching, redness, and swelling from skin conditions such as eczema, dermatitis, allergic reactions, and insect bites.
medicines.dosage: Apply a thin layer 1-4 times daily to affected area. Use sparingly on the face.
warnings: Do not use on infected skin without medical advice.
Avoid use on the face for more than 7 days.
Not for eyes, groin, or armpits.
Long-term use may thin the skin.
medicines.storage: Store below 25°C

medicines.name: Betamethasone
medicines.usage: Used to treat moderate to severe inflammatory skin conditions including psoriasis, eczema, and contact dermatitis.
medicines.dosage: Apply sparingly once or twice daily. Reduce frequency as condition improves.
warnings: Do not use on the face or in skin folds for extended periods.
Not for children under 1 year.
Avoid eyes and mucous membranes.
May cause HPA axis suppression with extensive use.
medicines.storage: Store below 25°C, do not refrigerate

medicines.name: Mupirocin
medicines.usage: Used to treat bacterial skin infections such as impetigo and secondarily infected eczema or wounds.
medicines.dosage: Apply small amount to affected area 3 times daily for up to 10 days.
warnings: For external use only.
Avoid contact with eyes.
Do not use for more than 10 days.
May reduce efficacy of some contact lens solutions.
interactions: Fusidic acid (synergistic — avoid combined use to prevent resistance)
medicines.storage: Store below 25°C

medicines.name: Acyclovir
medicines.usage: Used to treat herpes simplex infections (cold sores, genital herpes), chickenpox, and shingles.
medicines.dosage: Cold sores (topical): Apply 5 times daily for 5 days. Genital herpes (oral): 200mg 5x/day or 400mg 3x/day for 5-10 days.
warnings: Stay well hydrated to protect kidneys.
Not a cure for herpes — reduces severity and frequency.
Use at first sign of outbreak for best effect.
medicines.storage: Store below 25°C

medicines.name: Amlodipine
medicines.usage: Used to treat high blood pressure and angina (chest pain). Also used to prevent heart attacks and strokes.
medicines.dosage: Start: 5mg once daily. May increase to 10mg daily after 7-14 days based on response.
warnings: May cause ankle swelling (peripheral edema).
Avoid abrupt discontinuation.
Use with caution in severe aortic stenosis.
Avoid grapefruit juice.
medicines.storage: Store at room temperature, protect from light

medicines.name: Metoprolol
medicines.usage: Used to treat high blood pressure, angina, heart failure, and certain heart rhythm disorders.
medicines.dosage: 50-200mg daily (immediate release in divided doses, extended release once daily).
warnings: Do not stop suddenly — taper dose over 1-2 weeks.
May mask signs of hypoglycemia in diabetics.
Use with caution in asthma or COPD.
Avoid in severe bradycardia or heart block.
medicines.storage: Store at room temperature

medicines.name: Salbutamol
medicines.usage: Used to treat and prevent bronchospasm in asthma and COPD (reliever inhaler).
medicines.dosage: 1-2 puffs every 4-6 hours as needed. Exercise prevention: 2 puffs 15-30 min before activity.
warnings: Should not be used as primary long-term controller — seek regular asthma management.
Overuse may indicate worsening asthma — review treatment.
May cause paradoxical bronchospasm — stop and seek help.
medicines.storage: Store below 30°C, protect from frost and direct sunlight

medicines.name: Sertraline
medicines.usage: Used to treat depression, panic disorder, PTSD, OCD, social anxiety disorder, and premenstrual dysphoric disorder.
medicines.dosage: Start: 50mg once daily. Range: 50-200mg/day. Take in morning or evening with food.
warnings: Increased risk of suicidal thoughts in children and young adults initially.
Do not stop suddenly — taper dose.
Avoid with MAOIs (serotonin syndrome risk).
Monitor for unusual mood changes.
medicines.storage: Store at room temperature, away from moisture

medicines.name: Ranitidine
medicines.usage: Used to reduce stomach acid and treat heartburn, acid indigestion, GERD, and peptic ulcers.
medicines.dosage: 150mg twice daily or 300mg at bedtime. OTC: 75-150mg as needed.
warnings: Consult healthcare provider if symptoms persist despite 14 days of treatment.
Inform doctor of all other medications.
Note: Some formulations recalled globally due to NDMA contamination concerns.
medicines.storage: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture and light

medicines.name: Doxycycline
medicines.usage: Used to treat bacterial infections, acne, Lyme disease, malaria prevention, and respiratory infections.
medicines.dosage: 100mg twice daily for most infections. Acne: 50-100mg daily. Always take with plenty of water.
warnings: Do not lie down for 30 minutes after taking to prevent esophageal irritation.
Avoid sun exposure (severe photosensitivity).
Not for children under 8 (permanent tooth discoloration).
Avoid in pregnancy.
medicines.storage: Store at room temperature, away from light and moisture

medicines.name: Cilnidipine
medicines.usage: Treats high blood pressure (hypertension) and protects kidneys. It is a dual L/N-type calcium channel blocker, which reduces ankle swelling (edema) compared to amlodipine.
medicines.dosage: 5-20mg once daily, usually in the morning.
warnings: Monitor blood pressure regularly.
May cause dizziness or headache initially.
Use with caution in liver disease or heart failure.
Do not stop suddenly without consulting doctor.
medicines.storage: Store below 30°C, protect from light and moisture

medicines.name: Ketoconazole
medicines.usage: Treats seborrheic dermatitis, dandruff, ringworm, athlete's foot, and other fungal skin and scalp infections.
medicines.dosage: Shampoo: Apply to wet hair/skin, leave 3-5 min, rinse. 2-3x/week for dandruff. Tablets: 200-400mg daily (only under medical supervision).
warnings: Oral form: serious liver toxicity risk — use topical form when possible.
Many drug interactions with oral form.
Shampoo may cause temporary hair texture changes.
Avoid contact with eyes.
medicines.storage: Store at room temperature, below 25°C

medicines.name: Terbinafine
medicines.usage: Effective against dermatophyte (tinea) infections including athlete's foot, ringworm, jock itch, and nail fungus. Topical form kills fungi directly.
medicines.dosage: Cream: Apply once or twice daily for 1-2 weeks. Tablets: 250mg once daily for 2-6 weeks (nails: up to 12 weeks).
warnings: Oral form: monitor liver function.
Taste disturbances can occur with oral form.
Not for pregnant women (oral).
Avoid contact with eyes (cream).
medicines.storage: Store below 30°C away from direct sunlight

medicines.name: Calamine Lotion
medicines.usage: Provides soothing relief for itchy, irritated skin due to chickenpox, hives, insect bites, poison ivy, and mild rashes.
medicines.dosage: Shake well and apply to affected area using a cotton ball, as needed. Allow to dry on skin.
warnings: For external use only.
Avoid applying to broken or blistered skin.
Keep away from eyes.
Discontinue if rash worsens.
medicines.storage: Store at room temperature. Shake before use.

medicines.name: Adapalene
medicines.usage: Third-generation retinoid used for acne vulgaris. Regulates skin cell turnover, prevents clogged pores, and has anti-inflammatory properties.
medicines.dosage: Apply a thin layer once daily at night to clean, dry skin. May take 8-12 weeks for full effect.
warnings: Avoid sun exposure — causes photosensitivity.
Do not use with other retinoids.
Avoid waxing treated areas.
Can cause initial purging (temporary worsening of acne).
Avoid during pregnancy.
medicines.storage: Store at room temperature, away from heat

medicines.name: Tretinoin
medicines.usage: Gold-standard topical retinoid for acne and photoaging. Accelerates skin cell turnover, reduces fine lines, and treats hyperpigmentation.
medicines.dosage: Apply a pea-sized amount to clean, dry face at night. Start with 2-3x/week and increase as tolerated.
warnings: Severe photosensitivity — always use SPF 30+ daily.
Do not use during pregnancy (Category X).
Initial irritation common — start low, go slow.
Avoid with waxing or laser treatments.
medicines.storage: Store at room temperature below 27°C, away from light

medicines.name: Benzoyl Peroxide
medicines.usage: Kills acne-causing bacteria (C. acnes) on the skin surface and helps unclog pores. Available without prescription in concentrations up to 10%.
medicines.dosage: Apply to clean skin once or twice daily. Start with lower concentration (2.5%) to minimize irritation.
warnings: Can bleach fabrics and hair — let dry completely.
Avoid sun exposure.
Can cause severe allergic reactions (rare).
Avoid getting into eyes or mouth.
medicines.storage: Store at room temperature, away from heat and moisture

medicines.name: Azelaic Acid
medicines.usage: Dual-action treatment for acne and pigmentation. Kills acne bacteria, reduces inflammation, and inhibits melanin production for melasma/hyperpigmentation.
medicines.dosage: Apply twice daily (morning and evening) to affected areas. Safe for long-term use.
warnings: May cause temporary stinging/itching initially.
Safe in pregnancy (Category B).
Avoid contact with eyes.
May cause temporary skin lightening.
interactions: Generally safe; no significant interactions known
medicines.storage: Store below 25°C

medicines.name: Fusidic Acid
medicines.usage: Treats bacterial skin infections, especially those caused by Staphylococcus aureus, including impetigo and infected dermatitis.
medicines.dosage: Apply 3-4 times daily to affected area for up to 14 days. Cover with dressing if required.
warnings: Do not use for longer than 14 days to prevent resistance.
For external use only.
Avoid near eyes.
Not for widespread infections (use systemic antibiotics).
medicines.storage: Store below 25°C

medicines.name: Clobetasol Propionate
medicines.usage: Most potent topical steroid — for severe, resistant inflammatory skin conditions like plaque psoriasis, discoid lupus, and severe eczema.
medicines.dosage: Apply sparingly once or twice daily for maximum 4 weeks. Limit use to <50g/week for adults.
warnings: Do not use on face, armpits, groin, or under occlusion without specialist advice.
Risk of adrenal suppression with widespread use.
Do not use in children without specialist advice.
Not for acne, rosacea, or perioral dermatitis.
medicines.storage: Store below 25°C, do not freeze

medicines.name: Permethrin
medicines.usage: First-line treatment for scabies (Sarcoptes scabiei infestation) and head lice. Kills parasites and their eggs.
medicines.dosage: Scabies: Apply to entire body from neck down, leave 8-14 hours, wash off. Single treatment often sufficient. Repeat after 7 days if needed.
warnings: Itch may worsen initially (post-treatment inflammatory reaction).
Avoid contact with eyes.
Safe in pregnancy (with caution).
Treat all household contacts simultaneously.
medicines.storage: Store at room temperature

medicines.name: Levocetirizine
medicines.usage: More potent and less sedating than cetirizine. Used for allergic rhinitis, chronic urticaria, and skin allergy conditions.
medicines.dosage: Adults: 5mg once daily in the evening. Can be taken with or without food.
warnings: Less sedating but may still cause drowsiness.
Dose reduction required in kidney disease.
Avoid with alcohol.
Use caution while driving.
medicines.storage: Store at room temperature

medicines.name: Loratadine
medicines.usage: Non-drowsy antihistamine for allergic rhinitis, hives, and skin allergies.
medicines.dosage: Adults: 10mg once daily. Take on empty stomach or with food.
warnings: Avoid if liver disease (or reduce dose).
May still cause drowsiness in some people.
Avoid alcohol.
medicines.storage: Store at room temperature, away from moisture

medicines.name: Fexofenadine
medicines.usage: Effectively treats chronic idiopathic urticaria and seasonal allergic rhinitis. Does not cross blood-brain barrier — practically non-sedating.
medicines.dosage: 120mg once daily (rhinitis) or 180mg once daily (urticaria). Take on empty stomach.
warnings: Avoid taking with fruit juice (grapefruit, orange, apple — reduces absorption).
Antacids containing aluminum/magnesium reduce absorption.
Dose adjustment in severe kidney disease.
medicines.storage: Store at room temperature

medicines.name: Miconazole
medicines.usage: Broad-spectrum antifungal cream/powder for treating ringworm, athlete's foot, jock itch, and yeast skin infections.
medicines.dosage: Apply to affected area twice daily. Continue for 2 weeks after symptoms clear.
warnings: For external use only.
Avoid contact with eyes.
Inform doctor if pregnant.
May cause local irritation.
interactions: Warfarin (topical use — monitor INR if extensive use)
medicines.storage: Store at room temperature, below 25°C
